title: Workshop Tools, Fasteners & PPE: Present Simple & Imperatives
description: Essential English for identifying assembly tools, fasteners, safety gear, and giving simple workshop instructions.
learning_objectives: Use simple imperatives for safe workshop instructions (wear, check, tighten)
Apply basic present simple verbs for tool usage
Avoid basic Czech word order and pronoun omission errors

questions.prompt: Always _____ safety goggles before you start grinding the chassis weld.

explanations.correct: Imperative sentences use the base form of the verb ('wear') without '-ing' or 'to'.
explanations.wrong_A: '-ing' form cannot be used as a command or instruction.
explanations.wrong_C: 'wears' is third person singular, not an imperative command.
explanations.wrong_D: Infinitive with 'to' cannot be used for direct instructions.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech uses the imperative 'Noste / Mějte nasazené'. In English, simply use the base verb 'Wear'.

questions.prompt: Where _____ the pneumatic torque wrench for the wheel hub bolts?

explanations.correct: For singular noun 'wrench', the simple question is 'Where is the wrench?'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Where is located the wrench' has incorrect inverted word order for basic English.
explanations.wrong_D: 'does' requires another main action verb like 'Where does the wrench go?'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech word order is 'Kde je utahovák?'. In English, keep it simple: 'Where is the [item]?'.

questions.prompt: The assembly technician _____ all M16 bolts to 250 Nm every morning.

explanations.correct: Third person singular subject ('The technician') requires '-s' on the verb in Present Simple ('tightens').
explanations.wrong_D: Participle '-ing' alone cannot be the main verb.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czechs frequently forget the third person singular '-s' (*He tighten* instead of *He tightens*).

questions.prompt: Do not _____ the hydraulic lifting table while the warning light is red!

explanations.correct: Negative imperative 'Do not' is followed by the bare base form ('move').

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Nehýbejte s...'. In English, always use 'Do not + base form'.

questions.prompt: Our workshop _____ three overhead cranes for heavy chassis frames.

explanations.correct: Singular subject 'Our workshop' takes 'has' for possession in Present Simple.
explanations.wrong_A: Stative verb 'have' (possession) is not used in continuous aspect.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Naše dílna má'. Remember singular subject takes 'has', not 'have'.

questions.prompt: _____ these oil containers into the hazardous waste area immediately.

explanations.correct: Direct imperative begins with base verb 'Take'.
explanations.wrong_B: Participle '-ing' cannot initiate an imperative command.
explanations.wrong_C: Third-person form cannot initiate a command.
explanations.wrong_D: Adding 'You' makes it an unusual declarative sentence rather than a standard SOP instruction.

questions.cz_learning_point: In English instructions and SOPs, start directly with the verb: 'Take / Put / Check'.

questions.prompt: The apprentice _____ how to operate the pneumatic riveting tool yet.

explanations.correct: Negative Present Simple for singular subject is 'doesn't + base form' ('doesn't know').
explanations.wrong_A: 'doesn't' already carries the third person marker, so verb remains base 'know', not 'knows'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'neví'. In English, never say *he doesn't knows* or *he not know*. Use 'doesn't know'.

questions.prompt: _____ safety shoes required in this assembly hall?

explanations.correct: 'Safety shoes' is plural, so the question begins with 'Are'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Do' cannot be used with passive participle/adjective 'required' without another verb.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Jsou bezpečnostní boty povinné?'. 'Shoes' is plural in English $ightarrow$ 'Are safety shoes...?'.

questions.prompt: Please _____ the oil level before starting the diesel test bench.

explanations.correct: 'Please' is followed by the base imperative verb form ('check').

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Prosím zkontrolujte...'. In English, 'Please + base verb' ('Please check').

questions.prompt: This torque wrench _____ accurate to within 2 Newton-meters.

explanations.correct: Singular subject 'wrench' takes 'is' with the adjective 'accurate'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'have' cannot connect subject to an adjective.
explanations.wrong_D: 'has' cannot connect subject to an adjective.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Tento klíč je přesný'. Subject 'wrench' is singular $ightarrow$ 'is accurate'.
